 Judgment

1. The present appeal has been instituted by the appellant/complainant assailing the judgment dated 07.04.2025 passed by the Ld. JMFC-08, South-East District, Saket Courts (in CC No.
619780/2016) whereby the respondents were acquitted.

1
2. I have heard the submissions advanced by Ld. Counsel for the appellant as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents at length.

The entire trial court record, including oral and documentary evidence,
has been carefully perused.
3. The case of the complainant, in essence, is that the respondents induced her in the year 2005 to purchase a parcel of land purportedly situated in Okhla Village.

It is alleged that various documents,
namely Agreement to Sell, General Power of Attorney, Affidavit, Will and Possession Letter, were executed in her favour upon payment of 50,000/-.
Subsequently, the complainant claims to have discovered that the land in question belonged to the Irrigation Department.
Allegations of criminal intimidation, assault and trespass were also levelled against the respondents.
CA No. 240/2025 Fameeda Begum Vs. Azhar Hussain and Ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 2 of 7 4.
During trial, the complainant examined herself and her husband as principal witnesses.

However,
no independent public witness or any competent official from the concerned revenue or irrigation department was examined to substantiate the ownership, identity, or location of the alleged property.
5. The Ld. Trial Court, upon a comprehensive appreciation of evidence, returned findings which may be summarised as follows:
The complainant failed to establish with certainty the identity of the property allegedly sold.
There was no cogent evidence linking the property to the khasra number subsequently alleged.
Documentary material regarding government ownership remained unproved in accordance with law.
Material inconsistencies existed between oral testimony and documentary record.
Allegations of assault and intimidation lacked reliable corroboration.
Crucially, the element of dishonest intention at the inception of the transaction was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
5.1 On these premises, the accused were extended the benefit of doubt and acquitted.
CA No. 240/2025 Fameeda Begum Vs. Azhar Hussain and Ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 3 of 7 6.

The appellant has assailed the impugned judgment on the grounds that the Trial Court misread the evidence, adopted a hyper- technical approach, and failed to appreciate that the testimony of the complainant was sufficient to establish inducement and cheating.

It was argued that in view of the FSL report, the signature /
thumb impression of accused on documents in question got proved which falsified the defence of accused that they never executed the document in question.
It was further submitted that the impugned judgment is perverse in nature and is liable to be set aside.

Fameeda Begum vs Azhar Hussain on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179324997/
2 7.
Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the respondents has supported the impugned judgment, contending that the same is well-reasoned, based on sound appreciation of evidence, and warrants no interference.
8. Before proceeding further, it is apposite to reiterate the settled legal position governing appeals against acquittal.
The appellate court is required to exercise restraint and ought not to interfere unless the findings recorded by the trial court are perverse, manifestly illegal, or wholly unreasonable.
Where two views are reasonably possible, the one favouring the accused must prevail.

9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bhupatbhai & Ors. vs State of Gujarat has categorically held that an appellate court should not substitute its own view merely because another view is possible, so long as the view taken by the trial court is a plausible one based on CA No. 240/2025 Fameeda Begum Vs. Azhar Hussain and Ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 4 of 7 evidence.
10. Applying the aforesaid principle, this Court finds that the central issue in the present case relates to the identity and ownership of the land allegedly sold.

However, in considered view of this Court,
the complainant's case suffers from significant evidentiary gaps in this regard.
11. Admittedly, no revenue official was examined, nor were the RTI replies or documents pertaining to government ownership proved in accordance with law.

In absence of such foundational evidence,
the allegation that the land belonged to a government department remains unsubstantiated.
The Trial Court was therefore justified in holding that suspicion, however strong, cannot substitute legal proof.
12. Further, for an offence under Section 420 IPC, it is imperative to establish fraudulent or dishonest intention at the very inception of the transaction.

The material on record, at best,
discloses a dispute regarding title or identification of property.
Such disputes are predominantly civil in nature and cannot, in the absence of clear mens rea, be elevated to the status of criminal offences.
13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in G. Sagar Suri vs State of U.P. has cautioned against converting purely civil disputes into criminal proceedings as a means of exerting pressure.

sentences.text: Similarly, in Indian Oil CA No. 240/2025 Fameeda Begum Vs. Azhar Hussain and Ors. Page No. 5 of 7 Corporation vs NEPC India Ltd., the Apex Court deprecated the growing tendency to give criminal colour to civil disputes for oblique purposes.

entities.text: Indian Oil CA No. 240/2025 Fameeda Begum Vs. Azhar Hussain and Ors. Page No. 5 of 7 Corporation vs NEPC India Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. The present case appears to fall squarely within the said category.
The allegations primarily disclose a contractual/property dispute, for which the appropriate remedy lies before a competent civil forum.
15. As regards the allegations of assault and criminal intimidation, the Trial Court has rightly observed that the same are not supported by reliable evidence.

The medical evidence is inconclusive,
no independent witnesses were examined, and there are material inconsistencies and delay in the allegations.

The doubt entertained by the Trial Court in this regard cannot be said to be Fameeda Begum vs Azhar Hussain on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179324997/
3 unreasonable.
16.
While it is trite that conviction can be based on the sole testimony of a complainant, such testimony must be of sterling quality and inspire confidence.
In the present case, the Trial Court has found material contradictions and lack of corroboration on vital aspects, thereby rendering the testimony insufficient to sustain conviction.
17. A careful reading of the impugned judgment reveals a detailed, reasoned, and balanced appreciation of the entire evidence on record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page No. 6 of 7
The conclusions drawn therein are neither perverse nor contrary to settled principles of criminal jurisprudence.
18. The presumption of innocence, which is a cornerstone of criminal law, stands further reinforced by an order of acquittal.
Unless compelling and substantial reasons exist, such findings ought not to be disturbed.

19. In the considered opinion of this Court, the appellant has failed to demonstrate any perversity,
illegality, or material irregularity in the impugned judgment warranting interference.
20.
Consequently, the present appeal being devoid of merit stands dismissed.
21. Trial Court Record be sent back along with a copy of this judgment.
